cells.tense: You are here before any choice has landed, and the light is already doing its work.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Take what you are in the middle of and draw its shape on a page — no names, no events. Then set the page down and start nothing new.
cells.core:
You are standing in the open, before anything has been chosen, and it is showing — not because you are performing it, but because nothing is being held back. Anyone near you can feel it, and you are not doing it for them. Everything is still possible and you are inside that, not above it. The shine is not a reward and not a personality. It is what a thing does when it is not being managed.

What comes next is tracing the pattern you are already living. Draw the shape of one situation with the details stripped away and you get the mechanism instead of the story. That keeps the light from tangling in specifics. Tomorrow the pattern is clearer than it is today, and you will not need anyone to confirm it. The shine takes care of itself once the shape is honest.
cells.sheetLine: The light is on and you are not managing it.
cells.place: in the open before anything has chosen yet

cells.tense: Before the thing has asked to be chosen, you will have already declared what it is.
cells.act: leave it undecided a while longer
cells.ask: Something you have already decided the ending for — leave it undecided for three days, no verdict, no plan, no label. Let it sit.
cells.core:
The light is bright and it is running past the thing it is meant to light. You know what this is before it has arrived. The decision comes down early, the plan is built before the ground is walked, and the room gets glare instead of warmth. The shine is real — it is just standing in front of the thing rather than on it.

What is absent is the open moment before the choice lands. Leave one thing undecided and do not close the door early. You do not have to enjoy the waiting. On the third day you will know whether the waiting was hard or the deciding was. Either way the light falls on the thing itself again, and nothing is standing between it and the room. The brightness does not go anywhere.
cells.sheetLine: The light is proud and it is outrunning the work.
cells.place: in the open before anything has chosen yet

cells.tense: The thing you already are has already happened, and you are still standing at a door.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Point at one finished piece of your work and mean it — hold it at full size when the question comes, no softening. Just that, once.
cells.core:
There is a light in you and it has been getting called nothing. What is already made gets described as a small thing. What you can clearly do gets handed back with a shrug. The work is real and it is finished, and you stand in front of it saying it does not count. That is not humility. It is a dimmer switch, and your hand stays on it.

Take one thing that is already done and mean the sentence. Not a speech, not a boast — one clear line when the question comes. This, not that, asks nothing of how you feel first. You do not have to believe it. You only have to stop taking the shine off it. The thing is still there, already finished, waiting for you to stop standing between it and the room.
cells.sheetLine: You are dimming something that is already finished.
cells.place: in the open before anything has chosen yet

cells.tense: The light is on and the hand that set it there is missing from your account of the day.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: When the next new thing reaches you — a knock, a message, a turn in the road — meet it without folding it into what already happened. Just receive it.
cells.core:
You are shining and you have not noticed, or you are shining and something has stopped, and from inside it reads the same. The light is doing its work through your hands and the story you tell has no light in it. Anyone watching can see it before you can. They are not asking out of politeness — they can tell the difference between what you are doing and what you think you are doing.

What is arriving is the way back. Meet the next thing as it comes — the knock, the message, the turn — without making it a continuation of the old one. You are not adding to a story, you are receiving a new one. Met on time, the light has somewhere to land that is here instead of back there. You do not have to name what you are doing. You only have to be at the door when it comes.
cells.sheetLine: The light is on and you are not in the story.
cells.place: in the open before anything has chosen yet

It does not support: any claim about what the person has actually been doing in their life, how long anything has been true, or what they feel about it. The reader could reasonably object that I am describing a mood, not a behavior — so each core keeps the mechanism in a moment they could recognise and drops the cause. The sentence that serves me more than them is the opening of any Too Much cell that names 'the future' as a place they live — cut that, leave the moment where the drift shows.
